title: Why Ivie Anderson, not May Alix
summary: Greer repeats the story of choosing Ivie because May Alix looked white.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: That's right. No, no, the only thing Duke kind of drew the line on, that's how we got Ivie, you see, May Alex, the girl I was telling you about, the singer, a very -- she come to New York and was a sensation. But she was a girl, you couldn't tell if she was white or colored.
Oh, yeah, you told me about that. That's why he had to get Ivy Anderson.
So, when we got to Chicago, to open this theater in Chicago --

On our way West -- I'm telling it again. Anyway, Irving Mills is our manager. He said, I like that May Alex. So Duke say, "What do you think, Man?" I say, "Man, we look like hell with somebody who looks like a white girl standing in front of our band.
